t: Reverse Proxy Configurator - Signature build-tool concept
title: Reverse Proxy Configurator - Signature build-tool concept
definition: Routes requests to appropriate backend services.
description:
Reverse Proxy Configurator is the Signature build-tool concept that routes requests to appropriate backend services. In the Signature line, it is not a loose collection of scripts but a deterministic capability: the same build request produces the same verified result on every run, on every machine. This database documents the concept in full - what it is, the seven framework pillars that implement it, the real techniques it stands on, the standards it honors, and laddered drills that teach it from first principles to compounded mastery.

An AI that builds on demand needs Reverse Proxy Configurator the way a workshop needs its central bench. Without it, every build becomes improvisation: requirements drift, steps run out of order, and nobody can say why a result came out the way it did. With it, the build becomes a protocol - inputs declared, transformations explicit, outputs checked against the original request. That protocol is what these records describe, pillar by pillar.

Every record in this database carries a runnable demonstration program, because a build tool that cannot show its work cannot be trusted with real work. Read the overview, study the pillars, practice the drills, and run the demos: by the end the Reverse Proxy Configurator will be a capability you can invoke, not a concept you have read about.

t: Signature Provisioner - Reverse Proxy Configurator framework pillar
title: Signature Provisioner - Reverse Proxy Configurator framework pillar
definition: The Provisioner component of the Signature Reverse Proxy Configurator framework, owning provisioner. Signature concept.
description:
The Provisioner is a load-bearing component of the Signature Reverse Proxy Configurator framework. Its contract is narrow and absolute: within the framework, everything concerning the framework's provisioner responsibilities belongs to the Provisioner, and the Provisioner answers for it. This separation is what makes the framework testable - the Provisioner can be exercised alone, with declared inputs and checkable outputs, long before it is wired into a full build.

In operation the Provisioner works like this. A build request arrives carrying the Reverse Proxy Configurator charter (routes requests to appropriate backend services.). The Provisioner reads its portion of the charter, performs its transformation, and hands a verified intermediate result to the next pillar. If its checks fail, it stops the line and reports exactly what was wrong, instead of passing corruption downstream. That fail-fast discipline is the Signature line's signature.

Signature-concept illustration: a builder asks for a small cloud job that needs Reverse Proxy Configurator. The Provisioner takes the request's provisioner responsibilities slice, applies the framework's deterministic procedure, and returns its result with a proof of what it did. Run this record's demo program to see the Provisioner's core logic execute on a concrete example - the same logic, the same result, every run.

Signature framing: this pillar is part of the Signature line's original design for Reverse Proxy Configurator. It is labeled a Signature concept throughout - an engineered proposal, not an established public fact. The techniques it relies on are real and cited in the technique records of this database.

t: Signature Scaler - Reverse Proxy Configurator framework pillar
title: Signature Scaler - Reverse Proxy Configurator framework pillar
definition: The Scaler component of the Signature Reverse Proxy Configurator framework, owning scaler. Signature concept.
description:
The Signature Reverse Proxy Configurator framework decomposes the capability (Routes requests to appropriate backend services.) into seven pillars, and the Scaler is the one that owns the framework's scaler responsibilities. Owning a responsibility means three things in the Signature line: the pillar declares exactly what it accepts, it publishes exactly what it guarantees, and it logs enough evidence that a third party can replay its work and reach the same conclusion.

This discipline pays off when builds go wrong, because they always eventually do. When a Reverse Proxy Configurator result looks suspicious, the auditor does not re-run the whole build and hope; they replay the Scaler's log, check its guarantees against its inputs, and find the fault at its source. The pillar is thus both a worker and a witness - it does the work and it testifies about the work.

Try it yourself: this record's demo runs the Scaler's core procedure on a worked example. The program is plain JavaScript - save it as demo.js and run it with node, or press Run in the Demo Lab. Change the inputs and re-run; the procedure is deterministic, so you can verify every claim the description makes.
